title: Zscaler platform pillars: Zero Trust Exchange, Data Fabric for Security, Agentic SecOps and the customer-segment framing

prose.text: Zero Trust Exchange, Data Fabric for Security and Agentic SecOps are marketing pillars, not products; the customer-segment framing sits beside them.
Whether the platform is a unified policy and enforcement plane under every product is open {{gap:zte-plane}}.
{{dfs-exposure}} The Exposure Management products themselves are in [[aem.overview]], [[uvm.overview]], [[risk360.overview]] and [[easm.findings]].
How Agentic SecOps sits across the suite is in [[portfolio.security-operations]].
The four-pillar segment framing is resolved {{gap:segment-pillars}}: the page has no Branch pillar, and it lists use cases instead {{zte-use-cases|ref}}. The B2B segment is in [[portfolio.b2b]].

checks.do: For a question about what the platform unifies, answer from the platform claims and do not extend them to a policy plane under every product.
For a question about Agentic SecOps accuracy, present the figure as what Zscaler markets or claims, not as measured fact.

zte-platform.statement: Zscaler presents the Zero Trust Exchange as a comprehensive, integrated platform, with a proxy architecture that supports full TLS/SSL inspection at scale and brokers direct connections between users and applications based on identity, context and business policies.

quotes: as a comprehensive, integrated platform enabling zero trust security transformation
employs a unique proxy architecture supporting full TLS/SSL inspection at scale
brokering direct connections between users and applications based on identity, context, and business policies

zte-model.statement: The platform implements sequential verification in four stages: Verify Identity, Determine Destination, Assess Risk and Enforce Policy.

zte-signals.statement: Zscaler's marketing says the Assess Risk stage analyzes behavior and device status against 500 trillion daily signals.

quotes: **Assess Risk** - Leverage AI analyzing behavior, device status, and

zte-market.statement: Zscaler's marketing cites about 45% of Fortune 500 companies as users of Zscaler and a 2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant SSE leader designation.

quotes: 2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant SSE leader designation

zte-use-cases.statement: The platform page lists four use cases: workforce security, cloud and workload protection, IoT/OT connectivity and B2B partner access.

dfs-what.statement: Data Fabric for Security aggregates and unifies security data across tools and business systems, and the page says it is powered by Avalor technology from a Zscaler acquisition.

quotes: The Data Fabric aggregates and unifies security data across all tools and business systems
The Data Fabric is powered by Avalor technology (Zscaler acquisition)

dfs-integrations.statement: Zscaler's marketing cites 150 pre-built inbound and outbound integrations, and an AnySource connector for custom data sources.

quotes: with an "AnySource™ Connector" for custom data sources

dfs-targets.statement: The page names three target use cases: building CTEM foundations, creating comprehensive asset inventories and risk-based vulnerability prioritization.

quotes: Building CTEM (Continuous Threat Exposure Management) foundations

dfs-exposure.statement: The page says the Data Fabric forms the data aggregation backbone for the Exposure Management portfolio, which it names as EASM, Risk360 and Unified Vulnerability Management.

quotes: forms the data aggregation backbone for the Exposure Management portfolio, which includes EASM, Risk360, and Unified Vulnerability Management

agsecops-what.statement: The security operations page calls Agentic SecOps the AI-automation layer of its suite, and says its agents are trained on 11+ years of threat detection data.

quotes: trained on 11+ years of threat detection data

agsecops-accuracy.statement: Zscaler's marketing claims 99.7% threat accuracy for the Agentic SecOps agents.

zte-plane.title: Whether the Zero Trust Exchange is a unified policy and enforcement plane under every product
zte-plane.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'The unified policy + enforcement plane underlying all products.' The ZTE marketing capture calls the platform comprehensive and integrated but does not describe a policy plane beneath every product.

segment-pillars.title: Whether Zero Trust for Users, Workloads, Branch and B2B are customer-segment pillars
segment-pillars.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Zero Trust for Users / Workloads / Branch / B2B: the four customer-segment pillars. Maps to product groupings rather than discrete SKUs.' No captured page names these four segments; the ZTE capture lists use cases, not segments.
segment-pillars.resolution: The ZTE page lists four use cases (claim zte-use-cases) and has no Branch pillar.
